Subject: Handing off to Implementation — Brightline Pay SDK & cutover checkpoints

Sam — thanks again for the call this morning. This thread is the handoff to our implementation team so we can align sprint scope and cutover windows for the Brightline Pilot (MVP). Summary + immediate asks below.

Quick summary:
- Goal: Integrate Redwood hosted API for text generation + embeddings into Brightline Pay checkout and fraud pipeline; sandbox verification by Oct 15, production cutover targeted Oct 29.
- Important non-functional SLOs: p95 latency <= 220ms for single-turn text generation, embedding batch throughput >= 800/s for nightly jobs.

Immediate asks for Brightline:
1) Share a single engineering contact for API keys and sandbox ACLs (reply in line).
2) Confirm whether your sandbox environment will route outbound requests through your network proxy (we have a proxy-friendly SDK sample).
3) Upload a sample payload (anonymized) for typical generate/embedding calls so we can validate batching behavior.

What our team will deliver this week:
- A compact SDK quickstart (Node + Python) preconfigured with timeouts, retry policy, and a recommended token batching helper.
- Sandbox connectivity checklist and a one-hour joint verification session.
- A tolerance matrix to set client-side timeouts and server retry windows for your integration patterns.

Attachments included: brief SOW draft and sample config (attached to the next message).

Next step: if you confirm the engineering contact and proxy note, Marissa will schedule the joint sandbox session.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Thanks Sam — copying our implementation lead and infra engineer. I put together a compact verification checklist below and attached a small bundle (brightline-mvp-samples.zip) with: SDK quickstart (Node/Python), sample-config.yaml, and a small patch with timeout/retry examples (sdk-timeout-examples.patch).

Implementation kickoff checklist (first sprint):
- Sandbox access & API key: Brightline to provide QA key and whitelist list by Oct 4.
- Connectivity verification: joint session (60m) to exercise generate and embedding endpoints, confirm proxy headers and TLS handshake.
- SDK setup: developers should run the quickstart and verify 3 sample calls (generate, embeddings, health ping).
- Timeouts & retries: adopt the recommended default client timeout = 4s, retry backoff = [500ms, 1s, 2s], max retries = 3 for idempotent embedding uploads; for generate calls we recommend setting async fallback for prompts taking >6s.
- Batching: use the included batching helper to aggregate embeddings into 1k-item chunks for nightly jobs; use incremental checkpointing to resume failed batches.
- Rate-limits: Redwood will expose per-key rate-limit headers; client should react to 429 by backing off per Retry-After header and requeueing not-dropping critical items.
- Observability: enable token-level logging (redacted) and add a health ping metric (status endpoint) to your deploys.

Minimal SDK sample (Node.js) — included in quickstart, excerpt here:

const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, timeoutMs: 4000 });

async function sendPrompt(prompt) {
  try {
    const res = await client.generate({ model: 'rw-vicuna-1', prompt });
    return res.output;
  } catch (err) {
    // recommended: for non-blocking user flows, send to fallback queue after 3 retries
    console.error('generate failed', err.message);
    throw err;
  }
}

Operational notes:
- If you run into proxy-related TLS errors, switch the SDK to TLS SNI passthrough mode (see sample-config.yaml).
- For the nightly embedding job: implement a checkpoint file with lastProcessedId and idempotent upsert semantics. Our patch includes a small helper to compute batch fingerprints.

Schedule: I can book the 60m sandbox session for Oct 14 @ 10:00 PT. Vivek, Aditya — can you confirm who will join from infra/SRE?

Regards,

Subject: Re: Handing off to Implementation — Brightline Pay SDK & cutover checkpoints

Sam — confirmed for Oct 14 @ 10:00 PT. I'll join along with Aditya (infra) and one SRE. Quick operational guidance we will follow in the session:

1) Timeouts: Start with client-side default = 4s. If you observe consistent tail latency above 4s for generate, we will instrument KV cache warmup and increase endpoint concurrency rather than increasing client timeout by default.
2) Retry semantics:
   - Embeddings (idempotent): exponential backoff with jitter, max 4 retries.
   - Generate (not idempotent): do not retry blindly; instead, if a partial response is returned, surface to user with a server-side reconciliation job or fallback to secondary model that is cheaper/slower.
3) Rate limiting and 429s: implement a small leaky-bucket queue in the client; honor Retry-After header and tag requests with idempotency keys for batch uploads.
4) Monitoring: enable request-level tracing; we'll provide an OpenTelemetry sample to correlate Redwood request IDs with your logs.

Attachment: I uploaded the SOW draft and a short runbook to the Drive link above. We'll iterate on the SOW during the kickoff.

See you on Oct 14.
